learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the epic battle shaping our Earth! Learn how internal forces build mountains up, while external forces like rain and wind tear them back down.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Geomorphic processes are the forces that shape the Earth's surface. 'Endogenic' forces come from inside the Earth and build landforms up. 'Exogenic' forces come from the outside (like weather) and wear landforms down.
These are powered by Earth's internal heat. They include Diastrophism (slow movements like mountain building or continent uplift) and Volcanism (sudden movements of magma onto the surface).
Weathering is the breaking down of rocks IN THEIR PLACE. It can be Physical (temperature changes breaking rocks), Chemical (water dissolving minerals), or Biological (tree roots cracking rocks).
Mass movement is rock debris sliding down a hill due to gravity (like landslides). Erosion is the acquisition and transportation of rock debris by moving agents like wind, running water, or glaciers.

fun_activity.title: 🧊 The Freezing Frost Wedge
fun_activity.instructions: Fill a small plastic water bottle completely to the top, seal it tightly, and put it in the freezer overnight. The next day, the bottle will be bulging or cracked. This is exactly how 'Frost Wedging' (physical weathering) breaks solid mountains apart!

exam_tips: 📌 Orogeny is mountain building (severe folding/faulting), while Epeirogeny is continent building (gentle uplift/warping of large landmasses).
📌 Weathering is an 'in-situ' or on-site process—meaning no significant movement of materials takes place. Erosion involves actual transportation.
📌 Chemical weathering (like oxidation or carbonation) is most active in hot and humid climates.
quick_recap: ⭐ Endogenic forces build the Earth's surface, acting continuously from within.
⭐ Exogenic processes derive their energy from the Sun and act to level the land.
⭐ Denudation involves four phases: weathering, mass wasting, erosion, and transportation.
